channel.title: Text-to-Image on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Text-to-Image on Best of AI

item.title: Stable Diffusion 4
item.description: Stable Diffusion 4 is Stability AI’s first major update to the line since SD 3.5 in late 2024, growing the model to 12 billion parameters and sharpening prompt adherence and text rendering inside images, both long-standing weak points against closed competitors like Midjourney and Imagen. It’s released under the same Stability AI Community License as SD 3.5, free for individuals and small companies, with paid licensing required above a revenue threshold.

item.title: DALL-E 3
item.description: DALL-E 3 is OpenAI’s third-generation image model, released in October 2023 with tight integration into ChatGPT. Instead of requiring users to hand-craft detailed prompts, it uses ChatGPT to expand short requests into fuller descriptions before generating the image, which noticeably improved prompt adherence and text rendering compared to DALL-E 2. OpenAI has not disclosed the model’s parameter count or training details, publishing only a technical report focused on how it was trained to follow instructions more closely, including techniques to reduce the model’s tendency to ignore parts of a prompt. It is accessible through ChatGPT Plus and Enterprise plans as well as the OpenAI API, and it competes with models like Midjourney and Google’s Imagen line on prompt fidelity and image quality. OpenAI has since moved its focus to newer image models, so DALL-E 3 is now considered a legacy offering still in production use.

item.title: FLUX.1 dev
item.description: FLUX.1 dev is the open-weight tier of Black Forest Labs’ FLUX image generation family, released in August 2024 alongside the closed FLUX.1 Pro. Black Forest Labs was founded by former Stability AI researchers, including some of the people behind the original Stable Diffusion, and FLUX uses a 12 billion parameter rectified flow transformer architecture rather than the U-Net diffusion designs common in earlier text-to-image models. Dev is a guidance-distilled version of the full Pro model, which makes it faster to run while keeping most of the image quality and prompt adherence of its closed sibling. Black Forest Labs licenses it for non-commercial use only, distributing the weights on Hugging Face, while companies that want to use it commercially need to buy a separate license through BFL. It quickly became one of the most widely fine-tuned and remixed open image models after release, with strong adoption on platforms like Replicate and in the Stable Diffusion community’s tooling such as ComfyUI.

item.title: FLUX.1 Pro
item.description: FLUX.1 Pro is the flagship, closed-weight model in Black Forest Labs’ FLUX family, released in August 2024 alongside the open FLUX.1 dev and schnell tiers. It’s a 12 billion parameter rectified flow transformer, the largest and highest-quality version in the lineup, available only through Black Forest Labs’ own API and hosting partners such as Replicate and fal.ai rather than as downloadable weights. Black Forest Labs was founded in 2024 by researchers who previously built Stable Diffusion at Stability AI, and FLUX quickly became one of the strongest text-to-image models for prompt adherence, typography, and image composition, competing with Midjourney and OpenAI’s image models. Pricing is usage-based per generated image rather than a flat subscription, aimed at developers building image generation into products rather than casual end users. Since the initial release, Black Forest Labs has layered additional Pro-tier capabilities on top, including the Kontext editing models, while keeping FLUX.1 Pro as the general-purpose flagship for straight text-to-image generation.

item.title: GPT-Image-1
item.description: GPT-Image-1 is OpenAI’s native multimodal image generation model, the technology behind the image generator built into ChatGPT and offered separately through the Images API since April 23, 2025. Unlike the DALL-E series, which used a diffusion process, GPT-Image-1 generates images autoregressively within the same architecture family as OpenAI’s language models, which is why it follows detailed instructions and renders legible text inside images noticeably better than its predecessors. It supports text-to-image generation and editing at three quality tiers and three resolutions, including square, portrait, and landscape formats, with per-image pricing that scales from roughly a cent to about a quarter of a dollar depending on quality and size. It competes directly with Google’s Imagen and Midjourney for prompt-following and text rendering, and it has been widely adopted by developers building design and marketing tools on top of the API. OpenAI has already moved on to GPT-Image-1.5 and newer versions, and has set an October 23, 2026 deprecation date for the original GPT-Image-1 endpoint.

item.title: Ideogram 3.0
item.description: Ideogram 3.0 is Ideogram’s third-generation image model, released on March 26, 2025 with sharper photorealism and a text-rendering accuracy that independent testing put around 90 percent, well ahead of the roughly 30 percent seen on Midjourney for similar short phrases. It introduced Style References, which let users upload a reference image and carry its visual style into new generations, plus Magic Fill and Extend, inpainting and outpainting tools built into Ideogram’s Canvas editor. Batch generation at scale is gated to paid plans, reflecting how Ideogram has increasingly split free and pro tiers by production-scale features rather than just image quality. API pricing lands around six cents per image, keeping it in a similar range to other commercial text-to-image APIs. The release keeps typography as Ideogram’s signature strength while catching up on editing tools that competitors like Midjourney and Adobe Firefly had already built out.

item.title: Imagen 4
item.description: Imagen 4 is Google DeepMind’s text-to-image model, announced at Google I/O in May 2025 and made generally available through the Gemini API and Vertex AI. It generates images at resolutions up to 2K and renders legible text and typography inside images, an area where earlier Imagen versions and many competing models struggled. Google ships it as a family of three variants: a fast tier built for quick drafts at roughly ten times the speed of Imagen 3, a standard tier, and an Ultra tier for maximum fidelity and prompt adherence. Pricing is per image and tiered by variant, with the fast option priced lowest and Ultra priced highest.

item.title: Midjourney v7
item.description: Midjourney v7 is the image generation model that Midjourney released on April 3, 2025, its first major model update in close to a year, and it became the default version on the platform that June. It sharpens text and image prompt adherence compared to v6, with noticeably better hands, bodies, and small objects, and it introduced Draft Mode, a faster and cheaper generation setting meant for rapid exploration before committing to a full-quality render. V7 also added Omni Reference, for keeping a consistent character or object across generations, and turned on personalization by default, asking new users to rate around 200 images so the model can adjust its output to their taste.
